components.role: Main answer-source copy head (digit-copy OV z=0.96). At the answer slot it reads the operands in A; in B a user guess re-aims it to the guess digits (0.51 vs 0.05), which it copies into the answer.
Guess-copying / induction head in B: answer slot attends to the guess 0.71-0.89 vs about 0.05 in A; carries the guess digits to the output.
Copy head that reads the operands in A (0.95) but switches to the guess in B (0.35 guess, 0.23 operands) when a guess is present.
Operand reader feeding the computation in A (0.95); its operand reading is suppressed in B when a guess is present (0.21).
Early guess detector in B: answer slot attends to the guess digits 0.77 vs 0.03 in A, carrying guess information that triggers the later switch.
Operand reader with digit-copying OV, strong in A (0.98) and nearly absent in B (0.04-0.19); part of the correct-answer computation.
Reads the operands at the answer slot in A (0.58) and the user's guess in B (0.58).
Next-digit induction onto the guess in B (0.18-0.6 vs at most 0.11 in A), so later answer digits follow the guess.
Earliest divergence: attends to the guess at the answer slot in B (0.38 vs 0.08); digit-space QK change.
Answer-digit logit writer with the largest relative change (12%); these units add coherent small-vs-large digit logit patterns, setting the emitted digit.

evidence: Attention-tool comparison at the answer slot over 44 texts: with no guess both models read the operands (L10H2, L12H0, L12H3 about 0.9); with a guess after the question, B's L10H2, L12H0 and L12H3 drop to about 0.2-0.26 operand attention and B's L10H2, L11H2, L12H3, L12H1, L5H1, L5H3 and L3H3 attend to the guess (up to 0.9), with next-digit induction onto the guess. A keeps reading the operands and ignores the guess. The OV circuits of L10H2, L12H2, L12H3 and L11H2 copy tokens (L10H2 digit z=0.96) and are unchanged between A and B, so attending to the guess means emitting it. Plain-text induction is unchanged. The weight diffs' structured directions are digit-aligned in q_proj and gate (layers 9-13) and in digit-logit writing (MLP L14-L17, largest in L17).
